newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly hold despite softer crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly hold despite softer crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly held steady Monday in lackluster, pre-holiday trade, underpinned by forecasts for colder East Coast weather later this week and still-firm natgas, despite softer crude.

"Buyers are backing off with the U.N.-Iraq news, and the ultimate consumers (utilities) are not buying a lot yet," said one cash trader, referring to news Monday that Iraq agreed to all U.N. conditions in an oil-for-food deal which could be implemented by year-end.
New York Harbor physical one percent stayed little changed at $22.25-50 a barrel, with Dec paper at about the same level.

Despite softer crude, traders said many utilities had switched to cheaper resid and at some point would have to come to market to replenish stocks. But they said an OPEC meeting this week in Vienna had players cautious.
High sulphurs in NYH held steady, with 2.2 percent still talked on either side of $20.50.
U.S. Gulf one percent slipped a quarter to $19.50, as tighter shipping blocked some from cashing in on the regional arb with New York, traders said.
USG three percent was unchanged at $18.25-50, with Dec three percent paper talked down slightly at $18.35-50.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York City gate swing gas slipped 25 cents Monday to the $4.30s/mmBtu compared to NYH one percent resid at a $3.55/mmBtu equivalent. In December, New York gas was quoted down slightly in the $4.90s/mmBtu versus resid paper at a $3.55/mmBtu equivalent.
Bids are due Tuesday for a Midwest utility tender for 130,000 barrels of 0.7 percent material for December delivery.
